$comment: The releases this project measures itself against, and the facts that identify them.
Read by the `Reference releases are intact` step in release-dmg.yml, which fails the
build if any of these tags disappears or moves to a different commit.
GitHub-side tag protection became available when this repository was made public on
2026-08-17 — rulesets need Pro or a public repository, and it is now the latter. This
check is kept alongside rather than replaced by one: a ruleset can stop a tag being
deleted, but it does not record which commit the tag is supposed to point at, nor the
digest of the artifact that was published from it. Those are the facts a fallback point
is actually made of, and they live here.
Three references. v1.0.5 is the floor, v1.0.9 closes the 1.x line, and v2.5.9 is the
current release, published on 2026-09-20. A release cannot record itself — the commit
it names is the commit that carries it, and no file can contain its own hash — so each
entry here is added by the commit after the release it describes.
v2.5.9 replaced v2.5.8, withdrawn on 2026-09-20 — release, tag and DMG. The same
to v2.1.0 through v2.4.0
on 2026-08-30, so the 2.x line is still represented by its head alone. A reference
cannot be re-cut, so the work that follows one takes a number of its own, and keeping
the list at three means retiring the release it replaces rather than letting both
stand. What that costs is named rather than hidden: a fault introduced this week is no
longer bracketed from below by anything nearer than v1.0.9. The list is kept at three
deliberately; the next reference worth adding is the first 2.x state after this one
that is worth falling back to, and adding it is a decision rather than a consequence of
publishing.
Adding or changing any value below is a deliberate act and shows up in the diff as one.

references.why: First release of the numbering that survives; everything before it was withdrawn.
The second reference: credits the corpus authors, bounds a download that had nothing but the disk to stop it, and is the recent state to fall back to rather than the floor.

The current release and the third reference. It replaced v2.5.8, withdrawn the same day, and the number moved for the rule rather than for an obstacle: a reference release is not re-cut, so work that lands after one takes a number of its own. What it carries over v2.5.8 begins with the font: the pages of the package name a stack the reading machine may not have, and until now the package relied on the reader owning it. The application bundle carries the seven faces it draws with, the package carries the one it cannot do without together with the terms it is distributed under, the inventory credits its author, and manifest.json stopped saying the package carries no font while it carried one — which is why the package now holds 23 940 files and hashes to 87c854bf…7d49 instead of 714d6f65…68a5. The documents themselves are untouched: the byte mirror hashes to 7cfcdce4…35d0 exactly as it did for v2.5.8 and back to v2.5.4, 23 936 documents in 663 folders. A run now leaves nothing behind whichever way it ends — the copy it made for itself goes on success, on failure and on cancellation, a cached archive is never touched, and a cancelled run no longer forgets the folder the reader chose. Four faults of reliability are closed, each by a test that failed on the code before it: the cache sweep deleted .part files this program had not written, a package missing a root file was read back as whole, an interrupted read lost a transfer that had only paused, and the logger was installed after the thing that logs. The window speaks Russian on every path — the core's own English sentence no longer reaches the screen under «Собрать не удалось», every failure code the wire carries has a sentence of its own, and a code without one turns the frontend suite red. An archive entry stored under CP437 is read as its bytes say instead of naming a package file after invented characters. Also here: rustls 0.23.45 for RUSTSEC-2026-0285, revisions 54–65 of the specification, and the release gate of 2026-09-19 — the first run of it to reach the image and the reader's path, and the first to say build.
